# Pulse task #2773: Plan shared sample identity, tags and library interoperability between Hex and Yield

Operation: 59bed3685940fd9a8867d092a32c1e9b
Assignee: PORTALSURFER (Pulse #1, GitHub ID 41680373)

PLANNING ONLY — user asks Astra for an architecture plan; no implementation, database conversion, product merger or user-data changes authorized by this ticket.

User intent: keep Yield useful as a standalone app focused on sample management, extraction and organization, while tightly coupling it with Hex. A future app merger remains an option, not the current decision. Align sample tagging/organization and schema/domain language early in Hex development so samples move or load between apps with essentially no effort. Future example: Hex can record frequent use of samples A/B while composing, and Yield can see those facts to support possible suggestions such as liking/favoriting; no automatic rating/favorite behavior has been chosen.

Astra read-only review requested: inspect current Hex and Yield identity/location/media records, metadata/tags/collections/favorites, extraction/derivative provenance, caches/analysis, project references and persistence. Recommend a shared domain/schema contract and ownership model, distinguishing shared meaning from a shared physical database. Compare shared library/versioned interchange/IPC/store options with writer/concurrency, offline/app-version, crash/recovery and permissions boundaries. Preserve independent applications and future integration options; do not introduce a daemon or server merely to share metadata.

Required plan output: current-source audit and exact references; compatible versus differing contracts; explicit authoritative shared metadata versus project-local usage facts/machine-local paths and permissions/derived caches; finite initial milestones for shared tags/organization and frictionless interchange, later usage feedback with stable identity/idempotency; genuine open product decisions, acceptance criteria and data-preservation strategy. Sample identity must handle moves/duplicates/derived samples according to explicit contracts, not assume a content hash solves all identity. Include native drag/drop/open/import/reference workflows and file-access rights where supported by evidence.

Constraints: Hex alpha allows breaking model/project changes without legacy-alpha migrations. This does NOT authorize destructive changes to Yield libraries/profiles, extraction history, backups or recovery data. Preserve existing repository histories, current native qualification and unrelated source work. No app build/install/restart or Mac execution from this planning request. Existing project-owned instrument-chain plan2756 stays separate.

Cross-project scope: Hex project2 and Yield project4. Live duplicate searches for Hex/Yield/shared schema/sample metadata found no matching interoperability plan. Astra assessment pending; coordinator will reconcile findings here with fresh revisions and link related existing metadata work rather than duplicate it.

ticket.title: Plan standalone Hex and Yield with a common sample schema and optional synchronized library
ticket.description:
LINK ONCE, CONNECT BOTH — ACCEPTED USER CONTRACT
The link action is symmetric: initiate from Hex OR Yield with the same effect. Once confirmed in either app, both are connected through the neutral library system; never require a second reciprocal link. Example: a user has used Yield for a while, installs/opens Hex, chooses 'Link to Yield' in Hex, confirms the library, and the neutral system records the shared connection so Yield recognizes it too. Reverse initiation behaves identically. An app that is closed discovers the committed link when next opened; neither UI must be running to complete a durable connection. Duplicate/retried link actions are idempotent and cannot create competing libraries/one-sided connections; linking status must reflect committed state, with explicit errors if unable to complete. Library selection/source-of-existing-content semantics remain deliberate under alpha/current-format policy; do not silently merge or delete unrelated media. Both standalone operation and explicit unlink/disconnect remain available. This is one optional shared mode with two entry points, not two independent directional connections.

USER-SELECTED LINKING UX — 17 October 2026
Provide a 'Link to Yield' button/option in Hex and a 'Link to Hex' button/option in Yield as the discoverable entry into optional shared-library mode. Both connect through the neutral ownership system; this does not transfer ownership to either application. Use the action to select/create/confirm the shared library, show link/connection state, and provide an explicit unlink/disconnect route under the planned current-format rules. Exact placement and secondary switching details can follow the app's existing settings conventions; no further ownership choice is needed from the user. Both standalone applications remain fully functional. Planning only; no linking implementation or database reset started.

CURRENT PLAN — ACCEPTED PRODUCT DIRECTION, ASTRA SOURCE REVIEW, AND ALPHA POLICY
Planning only. No shared-library implementation, database reset, app merge or installation has been started by this item.

Outcome and modes
Hex and Yield remain separate, fully functioning standalone applications. Neither requires the other app to be installed or running. Both speak a common sample-domain language and access a NEUTRAL library ownership system; neither UI owns the other application's data.
Default standalone mode uses independent private libraries. Optional explicitly enabled shared mode connects both apps to the SAME chosen library authority and keeps its common sample data synchronized, including edits while the other UI is closed. One-way export/read-only projection may be an intermediate deliverable, not the final synchronized mode.

Reuse Yield rather than rebuild
Use Yield's existing persistence/session seam as the first adapter boundary. Reuse cohesive implementations and their meaningful tests:
- yield-library/src/sample_sources/db/ and library/: source registration, bounded queries, metadata, transactions, vocabulary and receipts.
- db/write/source_writer.rs and library/owner: writer ownership, revision checks and command admission.
- yield-catalog: scan publication, watcher invalidation and metadata query machinery; analysis workloads remain optional.
- selected pure yield-core types/validation, separated from UI projection, browser focus, waveform interaction and audition.
- library/harvest*: derivation facts, parent/child relationships, source ranges and operation receipts; keep Yield-specific Harvest workflow distinct.
- relevant operation_journal/filesystem identity/recovery units, preserving current-operation correctness rather than rewriting them for naming alone.
Yield's library crate has no GPUI dependency but still contains app-directory, preference and operation concerns. Do not make Hex depend wholesale on Yield UI/session/design crates or expose SQL connections/internal retained writer handles.
Packages may initially live in Yield's repository and be consumed at immutable revisions; repository location does NOT grant Yield UI runtime authority.

Intended dependency direction
Yield frontend/session adapter and Hex library adapter -> common client + pure domain contract -> neutral library owner/backend -> reused storage/catalog implementation.
Standalone may use an in-process private owner behind the same interface. Optional shared mode uses a neutral local owner/helper launched on demand by EITHER app. Neither UI process becomes the permanent host whose closure invalidates the other's work. No always-running remote service or cloud infrastructure is needed.

Shared sample domain and boundaries
Shared: library/item identities, exact content revisions, registered locations, tags/categories/collections, explicit rating/lock curation, committed derivation/provenance, optional accepted usage facts and library-wide maintenance policy.
App-local: Hex projects/AssetIds/clip timing/warp/device assignments/project Undo; Yield browser/Harvest workflow state where app-specific; preferences, selection, caches and private recovery/profile internals.
A project binding references a library item plus admitted content revision; media changes must not silently alter a saved musical project. Paths and OS access grants are local locators/capabilities, not global identities. Analysis is derived, versioned data, not a replacement for authored tags.
Share schema semantics/validated commands, not arbitrary private tables or waveform/PCM cache files.

Source findings and identity requirements
Astra inspected Hex main ad6d5f9e3ea1805034ef9e582b1af1d07bf24b3d and Yield candidate59498e281c2178dcb99b8a5fa7a08647a9e1641c (remote Yield main separately observed02a9faeddc00cdf7850fcef9adc7a63b2cdd3a6d). Read-only audit is not runtime validation.
- Hex sample library is currently a bounded WAV-path index with disposable binary cache; project AssetId is project-scoped.
- Yield browser AudioFileId is path-based; source records use source UUID plus relative path. Neutral sample identity must be durable independently of a present path.
- Hex verifies SHA-256 file bytes; Yield scans BLAKE3 file bytes. Fingerprints must carry algorithm and domain; unequal algorithms are not evidence of unequal media.
- Distinguish item identity, exact content revision and location. Proven rename/move preserves item identity; authored derivative gets its own identity/provenance; identical independent duplicates do not automatically share curation. Ambiguous external moves require explicit resolution.
- Yield source tags preserve display labels with normalized matching; profile vocabulary has narrower ASCII token rules. Preserve current Unicode labels and explicit mappings, not lossy conversion.
- Yield rating/keep-lock semantics and six collection memberships are existing behavior to reuse. Shared collection names/library maintenance policy must be separated from app-local UI preferences. Rating commands do not implicitly gain permission to trash files; usage does not implicitly finish Harvest or change ratings.
- Existing native Yield file drags and Hex external audio import provide a starting handoff path. Add optional identity/provenance payload with file URL fallback and validation, not temporary preview PCM. Each signed app must establish its own file access; do not assume access grants transfer.

Neutral authority, concurrency and failure behavior
One owner per library serializes mutations and coordinates metadata plus filesystem operation states. SQL locking alone does not prove safe rename/extraction/recovery orchestration. Do not open Yield's private profile as a second writer.
Shared helper discovery/arbitration uses an OS-backed ownership lock, selected library ID and owner incarnation; stale socket/PID files alone are not authority. Simultaneous launches attach or retry safely.
Commands use bounded schemas/pages, revision preconditions and stable operation IDs. Successful synchronization means durable owner commit; after timeout/restart, query the original operation result before retrying. Committed revisions drive both client views; caches never become a second silent authority. No IPC, file I/O, locks or allocation in audio callbacks.
Define current protocol/schema handshake and refuse unsafe mismatches clearly. This is current-format correctness, NOT a promise to support historical app/database versions.
Unavailable service/media yields truthful unavailable or pending status; local project assets/playback and cached browsing remain usable where possible. Do not claim offline edits synchronized without implemented commit/conflict semantics.
Explicit enable/select/create shared library and explicit disable/disconnect or independent current-format snapshot. Neither transition implicitly deletes external media. Diverged independent libraries are separate authorities; any later merge/reconciliation is deliberate optional product work, not required alpha migration infrastructure.

Alpha policy — USER OVERRIDE FOR BOTH PRODUCTS
Feature completeness is the current goal. Hex AND Yield are alpha: BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY AND DATABASE/SCHEMA MIGRATIONS ARE EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE until a future release-readiness/compatibility commitment.
Allow breaking API/model/schema changes and fresh/recreated alpha databases. Do not require old readers, compatibility re-exports, historical data conversion, old-client support or preservation of obsolete alpha DB layouts as prerequisites for extracting/reusing the backend. Earlier proposals requiring legacy Yield adoption/migration are superseded.
No actual reset/deletion is requested by this planning item or the AGENTS-only rule change. Preserve external sample files and correct current-format transactions/recovery; no need to weaken current safety tests or infer permission to delete original media. App agents are updating/verifying both AGENTS.md files separately.

Finite implementation sequence (future focused canonical issues/PRs, not started here)
1. Common contract + Yield client adapter. First complete vertical slice: list sources, page sample metadata, assign/remove an existing tag, observe committed revision and refresh Yield via the interface. Reuse current backend and validation; choose current-format identities deliberately.
2. Extract reusable neutral domain/storage/catalog modules and tests. Separate .yield/profile/UI preferences from neutral library configuration; preserve supported current behavior. Fresh alpha DB format allowed; no legacy migration/re-export obligation.
3. Neutral owner packaging/transport. Private standalone owners and optional shared helper behind same client semantics; either app launches it, concurrent launch arbitration, current-version negotiation, crash/readback/recovery and revision notification.
4. Hex adapter + optional shared mode. Browse and edit common organization, correct cross-app refresh, explicit library choice, identity-preserving drag/import/reveal/reference/copy, mode switching/disconnect. Keep project/media admission and audio-engine ownership intact.
5. Optional usage feedback. Control-side durable outbox, producer/event identities and transactional deduplication. Initial facts can cover committed project references/removals and bounded real playback aggregates; save/reopen/graph rebuild/Undo/retry must not inflate usage. Expose facts/suggestions without silently changing favorites, rating locks or Harvest state. Privacy/local scope and counting/retention remain product decisions.

Acceptance
Each app alone; both together; either starts shared owner; either UI closes; concurrent edits; stale revisions; crash after commit before acknowledgment; unavailable media/service; duplicate command replay; current-protocol mismatch; switching shared/private without unintended media loss.
Golden fixtures and behavioral oracles for identity/content/location, Unicode tags, ratings/locks, collection names, provenance and protected-source rules; both in-process and IPC adapters meet the same supported-operation tests. Prove actual supported file operations: existing public APIs that return Unsupported are not delivery.
Identity-preserving sample drag/import/reveal and project reopening with other app closed; signed Mac folder/drag/external-volume access tested rather than guessed.
Repository-required exact-source local checks plus one serial optimized cross-app Mac acceptance session for future implementation. Existing unrelated/historical passing candidates do not certify future refactoring.

Remaining product details, not prerequisites for the current planning direction
Precise copy/reference default; explicit semantics for duplicate curation; shared-library selection/switch UI; optional usage event counting/retention and recommendations; supported shared media operations and explicit destructive-action UI. Independent standalone apps + optional synchronized neutral library is FIXED, not an open product choice.

Existing work to align, not duplicate
Hex2665 persistent tag model/taxonomy,2666 filtering,2667 tag editors;2679/W15 sample assets and voices;2756 project-owned instrument-chain plan remains separate. Yield current archival/native qualification remains separate. This plan does not authorize expanding those PRs silently.

--- PRESERVED ORIGINAL BRIEF AND DECISION HISTORY ---
LATEST ACCEPTED USER REQUIREMENT — OPTIONAL SHARED DATABASE MODE
Both Hex and Yield must be fully functional standalone applications. Users with both may explicitly turn on a shared database/library mode and have their common sample data completely synchronized. Either app must remain useful and able to work with the selected shared library when the other UI is closed; a one-way export or requiring Yield open for all edits is only an intermediate milestone, not the requested final state. Define safe shared authority/writer arbitration/version negotiation, enable/adopt/merge conflict handling, disable/disconnect behavior and data preservation. Synchronize the shared sample identity/tag/organization/provenance/usage domain, not unrelated Hex project structures or Yield private recovery internals. The UI experience may be 'shared database'; assess a suitable internal owner/backend/helper or explicitly proven concurrency model. No database changes or implementation authorized yet. Astra addendum requested to revise its initial Yield-open bridge recommendation around this requirement.

ACCEPTED PLANNING DIRECTION — 17 October 2026
The user clarified and accepted: for now Hex and Yield are two completely separate, independently usable applications. They should speak the same sample language and have clean interoperability for future uses. A common contract and explicit library ownership are the planning direction; this does not authorize a mandatory shared writable database, daemon, app merger, or a runtime dependency on the other app being open/installed. Define useful offline/disconnected behavior. Implementation remains unauthorized by this planning item.
